card.title: Competing Theories
card.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our wedding cake's gone: theft, accident, or the dog. I suspect theft.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on him. Get him outside before Mum sees.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. I'll take him; check under the table for crumbs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That icing's from yesterday. The crumbs lead into the cloakroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Theft leads again. Keep the dog here; let's see whether that trail ends at a dropped cake or somebody's coat.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 names theft, accident and dog, A3 switches to dog after icing, and A5 restores theft while testing the trail against accident.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's icing makes A3 change the lead and request crumbs; B4's old icing and cloakroom trail cause A5's revised search.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the dog out before Mum sees and B4 provides relevant evidence distinguishing old icing from current crumbs.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's two clues to reverse the dog-removal plan and investigate where the trail ends.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a missing wedding cake and explicit rival explanations.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's dropped-cake-versus-coat test gives the theory change a playable next action.
